entries.title: 101 Ways To Use AI In Your Daily Life
entries.author: Tina Huang
entries.summary: This document lists many ways to use artificial intelligence in daily life. The author organizes the use cases into productivity, work, personal finance, learning, career, and relationships. General foundational models, specialized agents, and vibe coding tools support these daily tasks.

entries.title: 27 Claude tips after 1,800 hours
entries.summary: This document gives best practices for Claude usage based on practical experience. It covers context management, tool selection, and prompt strategies. Users learn how to reduce token costs and improve output quality.

entries.title: 7 Ways To Cut Your Claude Code Token Usage In Half
entries.author: Sean Kochel
entries.summary: This video covers seven strategies to reduce token usage and context window size in Claude Code. The author explores tools and methods for auditing waste, using terse language, managing intent layers, clearing context via handoffs, maintaining markdown files, querying code graphs, and proxying terminal outputs.

entries.title: A Complete Guide To AGENTS.md
entries.summary: Large instruction files waste tokens and confuse coding agents. Keep the main configuration file small and use progressive disclosure for detailed rules. Place specific guidance in nested files or separate documents.

entries.title: Agentic Code Review
entries.summary: AI tools increase code volume but delivered value stays low. Reviewers now face high code churn and missing intent. Teams must tier review effort by risk and capture agent reasoning in decision logs.

entries.title: Ai Workflow
entries.summary: Stop using one artificial intelligence tool for all tasks. Use different tools for specific tasks. Each artificial intelligence product has one main strength. Switch tools when a task fails instead of using the same prompt repeatedly.

entries.title: Boris Cherny: We Cut 80% of Claude Code’s Prompt
entries.author: Y Combinator
entries.summary: Modern language models require an empirical approach that starts by deleting system prompts and rebuilding instructions line by line only when failures occur. Developers must un-hobble agents by assigning harder high-level tasks, providing verification mechanisms, and utilizing dynamic workflows or routines to orchestrate thousands of agents. Evals remain necessary to measure capability, but they saturate quickly and require frequent updates as model intelligence accelerates.

entries.title: Build an Agent
entries.summary: Language models use tool-calling to act as reasoning engines. You can build an agent with LangChain and LangGraph. The agent uses search tools and conversational memory. You can stream messages and tokens from the agent.

entries.title: Building effective agents
entries.summary: Successful LLM applications use simple and composable patterns instead of complex frameworks. Developers must choose between prescriptive workflows and autonomous agents based on task needs. Clear tool design and transparency improve agent reliability.

entries.title: Can You Detect AI? (Anti-AI Writing Guide)
entries.summary: AI writing detectors use pattern matching to find common stylistic habits in large language models. Writers bypass these detectors by changing sentence length, removing stock phrases, and reducing punctuation marks like em dashes. Specific word choices and uniform positivity also signal machine-generated text.

entries.title: Claude COWORK Full Course: Zero To Working AI Employee (2026)
entries.author: KJ Rainey
entries.summary: This guide teaches users how to set up and use Claude Desktop with local folders as AI workspace environments. It covers building structured markdown skills, managing context windows, and creating multi-step automated agent systems. The author emphasizes solving real personal and business problems rather than automating everything.

entries.title: 18 Claude Settings That Change Everything
entries.summary: This document lists eighteen settings for Claude, Claude Code, and the API. These settings help users manage memory, context tokens, prompt caching, and cost. Most users do not use these settings by default.

entries.title: I Built Claude OS — A System That Turns Claude into an Execution Engine
entries.summary: This document describes a system that changes Claude into an execution engine. Developers use structured infrastructure like commands, plugins, and Model Context Protocol servers to build software faster. A single well prompted Claude instance often beats complex multi agent systems. Use specific activation codes and builder validator workflows to reduce bugs.

entries.title: The 9-Part Anatomy of a Perfect Claude Skill (and the 2 Parts That Actually Matter)
entries.summary: Building a Claude skill requires nine parts, but only two parts control if the skill works. The description tells Claude when to use the skill. The never-do line stops the skill from running on wrong tasks. You can debug a skill by asking Claude when it uses that skill. Claude only reads skill headers until a task matches.

entries.title: Claude Writing Style
entries.summary: This test compares plain English prompts with Claude-style prompts using strict technical language rules. Different models change their output length and style based on the instruction format. Letting a model write its own system instructions creates a closed loop that shifts output style without improving quality.

entries.title: Create And Edit Canva Designs With Chatgpt
entries.summary: This document explains how to use the ChatGPT Canva connector. You can create personalized designs in bulk with AI agents. ChatGPT navigates Canva and fills templates with custom text variations. You must review and clean up the final designs manually.

entries.title: Database Of Top Ai Tools
entries.summary: This document provides a curated list of top artificial intelligence tools categorized by use case. It covers applications for audio, content generation, developer tasks, image generation, productivity, and video creation. Users can find specific software options for business and personal workflows.

entries.title: FULL 3 HOUR COURSE: Automate Your Business With Claude AI (2026)
entries.author: KJ Rainey
entries.summary: This document outlines a structured approach to building AI systems using Claude. It emphasizes defining clear inputs and desired outputs before prompting the model. Users organize projects using specific markdown files and folder structures to maintain clean context windows.

entries.title: Full Guide - Build Your Own AI Second Brain with Claude Code
entries.author: Cole Medin
entries.summary: Build a custom AI second brain using Claude Code and Obsidian instead of complex out-of-the-box tools. Use a memory layer inspired by OpenClaw with markdown files like soul.md and user.md. Implement strict security boundaries to handle the lethal trifecta of private data access, untrusted content, and exfiltration vectors. Use a structured PRD generation workflow to build the system incrementally in phases.

entries.title: Google Cloud Released OKF — Think MCP, But for Knowledge Instead of Tools
entries.summary: Google Cloud publishes the Open Knowledge Format version zero point one. This format uses markdown files to store static knowledge for agents. The system forms a knowledge graph with standard links. Agents read these files to get context without loading all data.

entries.title: Free AI Marketing Team with Google Pomelli
entries.summary: Google Pomelli is a free tool that creates a full brand kit from a URL or photos. The system generates product photos, a website, and social media campaigns in fifteen minutes. Users input a website URL or product images to build business data. The tool then builds a website and marketing campaigns from the brand kit.

entries.title: How Anthropic Engineers ACTUALLY Prompt Claude Code
entries.author: Austin Marchese
entries.summary: Anthropic engineers build modular AI skills instead of writing single prompts for repetitive tasks. A skill contains a title description, step instructions, and tools like Python scripts or APIs. Small composable skills chain together and improve over every session through continuous updates.

entries.title: How We Built Our Knowledge Base
entries.summary: The internal knowledge base connects people and systems to useful information. The system extracts data from existing platforms without forcing migration. A hybrid search approach combines full-text search, embeddings, inverse document frequency, and age decay. An LLM distillation step normalizes Slack threads into structured documents before embedding.

entries.title: How Do You Set Up Your Code Review
entries.summary: Generic code review prompts fail because they lack project intent and context. Effective AI review requires feeding the LLM the original specification, ticket description, and repo-specific policy files. Using a panel of different model families catches more defects than a single model.

entries.title: How I Automated My Finances with Claude AI (EPIC DASHBOARD)
entries.author: KJ Rainey
entries.summary: This video shows how to build a personal finance dashboard inside Claude using a custom plugin. The plugin includes skills for initial setup, monthly updates, and dashboard customization. Users load their bank transaction CSV files into a folder and run slash commands to generate live HTML artifacts that track spending, subscriptions, and budgets.

entries.title: How to create, review, and merge stacked PRs on GitHub | GitHub Checkout

entries.summary: GitHub introduces stacked pull requests to help developers break large features into smaller reviewable parts. Developers can manage stacks using the web user interface or the new command line extension. Multiple pull requests in a stack merge into the main branch with a single click.

entries.title: How To Make Codebases AI Agents Love
entries.summary: AI agents need clean codebases because they act like new starters with no memory. Poor codebase design causes slow feedback loops, hard navigation, and cognitive burnout. Use deep modules with simple interfaces and strong tests to help AI agents work better.

entries.title: How To Setup Up Claude
entries.summary: Build an AI workspace to save time on repetitive work. Use the desktop app and select the correct plan. Give Claude context about your business and goals. Organize your files and projects to improve output quality.

Notes act as standardized units or shipping containers for ideas that connect into a larger system. Users apply standardization rules, use backlinks to link visual components, and build a four-dimensional knowledge system.

entries.title: How to Use AI Agents for Total Beginners: A Crash Course w/ Agent Builder James McAulay

entries.summary: AI agents need three components to function: an LLM brain, context files, and software integrations. Users can build proactive agents using Claude Co-work or Claude Code combined with Model Context Protocol connectors and markdown instruction files. Setting up a second brain folder and specialized skills allows agents to execute routine business tasks automatically.

You upload reference images and paste a design prompt to extract a design system. Then you review a visual preview before you add your content. This method gives you precise and easily editable results.

entries.summary: Developers debate the relevance of the Superpowers skill set for Claude Code. Some users find high token costs and strict workflows unnecessary with newer, smarter models. Other users prefer extended forks and custom hooks to orchestrate multi-model workflows efficiently.

entries.title: Json Prompting
entries.summary: This document explains JSON prompting as a structured method for AI tasks. JSON prompting uses object formats to specify goals, constraints, and outputs clearly. This method replaces freeform text with precise machine-like instructions.

entries.summary: Moonshot released Kimi K3 open weights on Hugging Face. The model uses a mixture of experts architecture with a large context window. Self-hosting requires multiple high-end graphics processing units. Users can use alternative cloud providers if local hardware is insufficient.

entries.title: Management as AI Superpower
entries.summary: Management skills drive success with AI agents more than clever prompts. Users trade human baseline time against probability of success and AI process time. Subject-matter experts use clear goals, evaluation, and feedback to guide AI tools.

entries.title: ML Foundations for AI Engineers (in 34 Minutes)
entries.author: Shaw Talebi
entries.summary: Intelligence requires world models that compress reality to make predictions. Machine learning fits models to data using math and optimization. Deep learning uses neural networks to learn features from raw data automatically. Reinforcement learning maximizes reward functions through trial and error.

entries.title: Work Plan: Repository Reconnaissance & Skill Factory Partitioning
entries.summary: The document explains how to convert web browsing agent trajectories into standalone executable code skills. The system uses AST multi-solve alignment to lift hardcoded values into command-line arguments. Two-pass verification gates ensure that skills pass ground truth checks before deployment. A pre-agent routing system decides whether to execute a skill directly or use standard exploration.

entries.title: My AGENTS.md file for building plans you actually read
entries.summary: Use a four step planning loop to improve artificial intelligence code generation. Plan the approach with the artificial intelligence before you write any code. Execute the plan, test the result, and commit the code. This method stops hallucinations and makes the code better.

entries.title: My Job Posting Prompt
entries.summary: This prompt sets up an AI system as an executive-career strategist to build a truthful, evidence-based case for job applications. The workflow moves step by step from candidacy assessment and resume architecture to professional summaries, experience entries, and cover letters. The user reviews and locks each step before the system advances to the next stage.

This setup reduces token usage while maintaining relevant context across sessions.

entries.summary: PostHog shares five lessons on writing agent skills that work. The lessons cover progressive disclosure, avoiding over-specification, preventing skill rot, asking the agent for feedback, and choosing when to write a skill.

entries.title: Procoder
entries.summary: Procoder is an engineering discipline layer for AI coding agents. It enforces a structured software development workflow with blocking controllers. The tool uses a P-CONTROL principle where the binary computes data, the agent reasons, and the agent changes the code.

entries.title: Prompt Design Strategies
entries.summary: Prompt design is the process of creating natural language requests to get accurate responses from language models. You improve model behavior by using clear instructions, constraints, formatting, and few-shot examples. You can also chain prompts and adjust parameters like temperature to control output quality.

entries.title: Prompt engineering overview
entries.summary: This document gives an overview of prompt engineering methods for Claude models. You must define success criteria and test prompts before you start. Use the listed techniques in order when you troubleshoot model performance.

entries.title: Prompt Engineering
entries.summary: Recent academic studies show new rules for prompt engineering. Users must avoid tag questions and step-by-step instructions. Users must limit rules to three maximum and focus on clear goals instead of examples.

entries.title: Single Markdown File Memory
entries.summary: The author builds an open source tool named magpie. This tool saves all content that Claude reads or watches into local markdown files. The storage uses no cloud and works with Obsidian.

entries.title: The Agentic Engineer Workflow You Need In 2026
entries.author: Zen van Riel
entries.summary: The author shares a parallel coding agent workflow using four terminals with different effort levels. Engineers manage context windows by using compact or clear commands when conversation history grows too large. Git work trees allow independent work streams without branch conflicts across parallel windows. Professional engineering standards require architectural oversight and human review rather than uncritical code generation.

entries.title: Top Hidden Claude Commands
entries.summary: You can use prompt shortcuts as custom commands to avoid writing long instructions repeatedly. Build a small command library for tasks like research, criticism, and summarization. Define the exact behavior of each command instead of using simple keywords for better results.

entries.summary: Use visual-output prompt shortcuts to change the shape of a problem and find missing logic in plans. Request specific representations like flowcharts, timelines, and blueprints instead of generic infographics. Chain different visual formats to move from structure to execution and communication.

Many users find third-party memory plugins unreliable and prefer custom markdown file structures, dedicated handoff folders, or local databases. Instruction files like CLAUDE.md help enforce memory search before agents answer.

entries.title: Youtube Authorities
entries.summary: Users discuss problems with agent tutorial videos on YouTube. One user shares a practical method to run multiple AI coding agents in parallel. The method uses separate chat sessions, git worktrees, and concrete markdown files.

Users install the plug-in from community settings and combine it with featured image, style settings, and omnisarch plug-ins. The tool supports tag navigation, folder shortcuts, pinned notes, custom icons, and folder background colors. Users also can hide specific directories and use advanced search providers for full-text searches.

entries.title: How Anthropic Engineers ACTUALLY Prompt Claude Code
entries.author: Austin Marchese
entries.summary: Anthropic engineers prompt Claude using composable skills instead of repetitive custom prompts. Skills package procedural knowledge into folders containing descriptions, instructions, and tools like Python scripts. Users update skills continuously after each session to create a compounding improvement loop.

entries.title: LIVE: Uncle Bob on Software Fundamentals in the Age of AI
entries.author: Matt Pocock
entries.summary: AI agents suffer from messy codebases in the same way human developers do. To prevent agents from entering failure loops, developers must use automated, deterministic checks like code coverage, cyclomatic complexity scores, and mutation testing as hard quality gates. Forcing human behaviors like strict test-driven development onto agents fails, but enforcing human structural values through tight tools and modular architecture succeeds. Because the cost of change is now close to zero, traditional upfront waterfall planning should be replaced with agile, iterative agent execution.

entries.title: My Simple Claude Cowork System (for normal people)
entries.author: Jeff Su
entries.summary: Build a structured folder system for AI assistants to maintain persistent memory and context. The root directory contains master rules and memory files that point to specialized workstations. This architecture uses rule stacking and resources folders to keep token usage low.

entries.title: So I tried Matt's skills...
entries.author: Theo - t3․gg
entries.summary: Engineers build custom AI skills using simple markdown files. Developers audit existing skill suites from Matt Pocock and Lauren Porter to select relevant tools. The unslop skill removes AI writing patterns and produces human-sounding text. Users test skills directly by copying text into agents before installation.

entries.title: 'Software Fundamentals Matter More Than Ever' — Matt Pocock
entries.author: AI Engineer
entries.summary: Software fundamentals remain critical for AI-assisted coding to prevent code complexity and entropy. Developers must establish shared design concepts, ubiquitous language, and deep modules before generating code. Using test-driven development forces small, deliberate steps and prevents AI from outrunning feedback loops.

entries.title: When to Build Your Own Agent Harness | Harrison Chase, LangChain
entries.author: Sequoia Capital
entries.summary: Building AI agents requires owning three main components: the model, the context, and the harness. The harness orchestrates the model and context by bringing context into the model window at the right time. Developers can customize harnesses using middleware constructs like hooks and plugins to add capabilities such as sandboxes, file systems, sub-agents, and memory. Evals and observability platforms like Harbor and LangSmith power a continuous learning data flywheel to improve agent performance over time.
